story_subtitle: Analyzing the relationship between income, health, and population across regions

story_pieces.narration: Higher income countries generally exhibit better health outcomes, with nations like Norway (income: $64,304, health: 81.6) and Singapore ($80,794, health: 82.1) leading in both metrics, while countries like Burundi (income: $777, health: 60.4) and Somalia ($624, health: 58.7) show stark contrasts.
story_pieces.question: Is there a correlation between a country's income level and its health indicators?
story_pieces.visualization: scatter plot (income vs. health, colored by region)

story_pieces.narration: The Middle East and North Africa region has the highest average income ($20,816), followed by Europe and Central Asia ($22,615), while Sub-Saharan Africa has the lowest average income ($6,831).
story_pieces.question: Which regions have the highest and lowest average incomes?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (regions vs. average income)

story_pieces.narration: Population size does not directly correlate with health outcomes, as seen in countries like Chad (population: 14 million, health: 57.7) and Japan (population: 126 million, health: 83.5).
story_pieces.question: How does population size influence health metrics across countries?
story_pieces.visualization: bubble chart (population vs. health, size representing income)

story_pieces.narration: Sub-Saharan Africa has the lowest average health score (67.1) and the highest population variance, with countries like Lesotho (health: 48.5) and South Africa (health: 63.7) showing significant disparities.
story_pieces.question: Which region faces the greatest health challenges and population diversity?
story_pieces.visualization: ranked bar chart (countries in Sub-Saharan Africa vs. health scores)

story_pieces.narration: High-income countries with the best health outcomes include Australia ($34,186, health: 80.6), Canada ($43,294, health: 81.7), and the United States ($53,354, health: 79.1), while high-income nations like Qatar ($48,226, health: 75.7) and Kuwait ($82,633, health: 80.7) show mixed results.
story_pieces.question: Which high-income countries also achieve the highest health indices?
story_pieces.visualization: world map (countries colored by income and health quartiles)
